briefSection: TESTING — BE HONEST ABOUT WHAT A GUEST CAN PROVE (items 1-7)

environment.where: developer agent sandbox inside a Tamandua worker round (Matchlock guest)
environment.reason: a nested VM cannot boot in-guest; the sandbox runs NoNewPrivs=1 / CapEff=0, so matchlock's file capabilities are suppressed and the first VM create fails TUNSETIFF: operation not permitted
environment.consequence: no test recorded as 'executed' below is a real-VM test; simulated arms are labelled simulated

executions.note: counts are for the whole containing file; the file is host-side fs / worker-thread execution only, no VM and no guest
two-implementation invariant control (PRE_FIX model vs SHIPPED exports); its red evidence comes from a mutation probe that delegates SHIPPED to PRE_FIX, see items[5].redEvidence

items.requirement: Overlay roots for two concurrent invocations of the SAME run are DISTINCT and under the new parent.

provingTest.title: gives two invocations of one run DISTINCT roots

items.note: the derive test pins the disjoint versioned parent dsh-profile-invocations/<bareRunId>; the distinctness test pins that two invocation ids of one bare run never share a root

items.requirement: Cleanup of invocation A cannot remove or invalidate invocation B's live root, in BOTH teardown orders (A-then-B and B-then-A).

provingTest.title: merges two overlapping invocations' unique artifacts without loss in EITHER teardown order

additionalProvingTests.title: removes exactly the attested invocation root and is idempotent (empty group pruned, sibling invocations kept)
shipped lifetime arm: two distinct invocation roots survive the peer's cleanup and still accept new writes

items.note: the shipped lifetime arm also proves the surviving peer root still accepts NEW writes after the cleanup, i.e. it is not merely left on disk but still usable

items.requirement: A legacy per-run path is never used to delete a live invocation root (compatibility/migration behaviour, if the reference has any — read it, don't invent it).

provingTest.title: never touches a PRE-PLANTED legacy run-scoped root, through prepare AND cleanup

additionalProvingTests.title: attests exactly one invocation root and fails closed for any other path (including legacy)
refuses the LEGACY run-scoped shape as a mount source

items.note: the reference has NO migration/reclaim path: the legacy shape is never adopted, deleted or migrated. The pins cover prepare, cleanup, attestation and mount planning

items.requirement: Publication serializes, and a genuine conflict is retained and reported rather than lost.

provingTest.title: retains a TRUE conflict instead of silently overwriting an independently changed host destination

additionalProvingTests.title: serializes two genuinely concurrent finalizers: ONE winner + one retained conflict on a shared destination
keys the publication lock by the host home under the host-only live state

items.note: the conflict is reported as the typed dsh_profile_overlay_publish_conflict and the losing copy is retained on disk, never discarded

items.requirement: Contradictory teardown orders leave no artifact loss and no deadlock, including when a holder crashed.

provingTest.title: loses no artifact under EITHER teardown order (A-then-B and B-then-A; SIMULATED: no VM)

additionalProvingTests.title: loses no artifact when a CRASHED holder's lock is left behind under the reverse teardown order (SIMULATED: no VM)
breaks a CRASHED holder's lock and still publishes (SIMULATED crash: dead pid, no VM)

items.simulationNote: SIMULATED: the crash is a planted lock directory whose owner file names a positively-dead pid (proven ESRCH, above any platform pid_max); no process is killed, no VM and no guest is involved
items.note: no-deadlock is asserted both ways: a crashed (dead-owner) lock is broken rather than waited out, and an indeterminate owner is never broken

items.requirement: A REGRESSION CONTROL: demonstrate that the key test actually FAILS against the pre-fix behaviour.

provingTest.title: pre-fix lifetime arm: the shared run-scoped root teardown destroys the peer invocation's staged artifact

additionalProvingTests.title: pre-fix publication arm: the unconditional copy publishes the invocation's losing copy over the independently changed host destination
shipped publication arm: the typed dsh_profile_overlay_publish_conflict retains the independently changed host bytes and the losing copy

items.preFixState: The pre-fix implementation in the same file (PRE_FIX) models baseline f2f34c91: ONE shared run-scoped overlay root <liveState>/matchlock/dsh-profile-overlays/<bareRunId> adopted by every invocation, with an unconditional recursive teardown, and an unconditional fs.copyFileSync publish with no manifest/lock. Against it the pre-fix lifetime arm reproduces peer_artifact_destroyed (cleanup of invocation inv-aaaaaaaa-11111111 destroys invocation inv-bbbbbbbb-22222222's staged artifact .../dsh-profile-overlays/1111/sessions/regression/b/*.jsonl) and the pre-fix publication arm reproduces independent_host_destination_overwritten (expected "from-host\n", observed "from-invocation\n"). Red evidence for the SHIPPED implementation itself comes from a mutation probe that rewires the SHIPPED delegates to PRE_FIX: tests 5 / pass 2 / fail 3 with the messages above, after which the file was restored byte-identically (sha256 fface69f8da660ee1243c20e471e12ca3fb7159be41929700f901d61668c7efb).
items.note: non-vacuity is structural: expectViolation() calls assert.fail when a pre-fix arm unexpectedly satisfies the invariant, so the control cannot pass silently

items.requirement: The pre-existing overlay unit tests still pass.

provingTest.title: stages a private byte-identical copy of the host profiles tree

additionalProvingTests.title: exports the planner surface and imports only node: builtins

items.note: the PRE-EXISTING assertions were never weakened; the file reports 52 tests / 52 pass / 0 fail / 0 skipped, which is the pre-existing suite plus the additive arms added by this port

realMatchlockOverlapGate.title: keeps a live invocation across the peer's cleanup and publishes BOTH invocations' REAL new artifacts (both teardown orders)
realMatchlockOverlapGate.reason: cannot boot nested VMs in-guest; coordinator/host-owned
realMatchlockOverlapGate.note: the gate body, its two teardown orders and its event-loop-safe host waits are pinned structurally by tests/matchlock-dsh-overlay-gate-wiring.test.ts and its fixture controls by tests/matchlock-dsh-profile-overlay-gate-helpers.test.ts; neither pin is real VM execution. A green real run needs ./run-matchlock-dsh-profile-overlay-e2e-test (or the gate file under the shared gate lock) on the host outside the agent sandbox, and its artifact truth is profile-overlay-overlap.json in the gate evidence dir
